text.p: Brazilian shoemaker and textile firm Sao Paulo Alpargatas has named Alcides Tapias as the new president of its board, replacing Diego Bush, who has resigned, the firm said in a statement.

The decision was taken after the firm's major stockholders Bradesco and Camargo Correa, which hold 21.2 percent and 33.5 percent of the company, respectively, agreed that the firm should restructure and set new strategies, the statement said.
Tapias, who also is Camargo Correa's main executive, will be in charge of restructuring and strengthening Alpargatas operations and strategies to compete in an open economy, it added.
Fernando Tigre, a former director of Alcoa Aluminio and president of pulp and paper firm Jari Celulose, has been chosen to be Alpargatas' new executive director, the statement said.
Tapias and Tigre are expected to take office only by the end of the month after Sao Paulo Alpargatas' shareholders meet to approve the changes, the statement said.
Local pension fund Previ, which holds a 12.6 percent stake in Sao Paulo Alpargatas, is also mulling the idea of taking part in the restructuring plan, it said.
Sao Paulo Alpargatas sales in 1996 reached 594 million reais ($570 million), it added.
